paper_a.title: Regret Analysis of Stochastic and Nonstochastic Multi-armed Bandit Problems (Bubeck-Cesa-Bianchi 2012)

metadata.description: Paper A is a survey/monograph on multi-armed bandits and online learning, centred on regret minimization for sequential decision problems (UCB, Exp3/Exp3.P/Exp4, Online Mirror Descent, contextual / linear / nonlinear bandits, semi-bandit, two-/one-point feedback, unimodal stochastic bandits). Paper B introduces the Variational Auto-Encoder: a generative latent-variable model trained by stochastic gradient ascent on a reparameterized variational lower bound (ELBO). The two papers share no mathematical objects, problem statements, theorems, or algorithmic ideas: bandits operate on a discrete or continuous arm/action space with adversarial or stochastic loss feedback and minimize regret w.r.t. a best fixed comparator; VAEs perform amortized approximate posterior inference for a directed latent variable model and minimize a KL-regularized reconstruction objective. Even at the level of broad machinery there is no overlap (concentration / change-of-measure / Bregman-divergence regret bounds vs. change-of-variables / reparameterization for differentiable Monte Carlo expectations). The only superficial commonalities are generic stochastic-gradient style optimization and Monte Carlo expectations, which do not constitute a meaningful structural alignment. All paper-origin Level-1 nodes on each side are emitted as `none`.

matches.explanation: Stochastic multi-armed bandit problem: arms with unknown reward distributions, regret minimization. Paper B has no notion of arms, regret, or sequential exploration-exploitation; its problem is unsupervised generative modeling of i.i.d. data.
Adversarial bandit: regret against arbitrary loss sequences. No counterpart in VAE setting (i.i.d. dataset, no adversary).
Online linear optimization with bandit feedback. Has no analogue in the VAE generative-modeling setup.
Online combinatorial / semi-bandit optimization. Absent in paper B.
Nonlinear two-point bandit feedback problem. No counterpart in VAE.
Nonlinear one-point bandit feedback problem. No counterpart in VAE.
Unimodal stochastic bandit on $[0,1]$. No analogue in paper B.

Sub-Gaussian / cumulant moment condition on arm rewards used for UCB concentration. VAE makes no such concentration assumption on the data; its modeling assumptions are about parametric prior/likelihood differentiability, not tail behaviour.
Strong-mode / Lipschitz unimodal regularity for SGS. No analogue in VAE.
Legendre-Fenchel transform of a moment-bound function $\psi$. VAE never invokes Fenchel duality.

Bernoulli KL divergence used in the Lai-Robbins lower bound. VAE uses Gaussian-Gaussian KL (TP14.2) in a completely different role (regularizer in the ELBO, not a lower-bound proof tool); the two KL's do not correspond beyond both being instances of relative entropy.
Subdifferentiable function definition, foundation of OMD. Absent in paper B.
Legendre-Fenchel transform of a function. Absent in VAE.
Legendre function definition (for OMD). No counterpart in paper B.
Bregman divergence used as the geometry of OMD updates. VAE uses KL divergence in the ELBO but never invokes general Bregman geometry.
$\omega$-potential / $0$-potential family for OSMD regularizers. Absent in paper B.
Definitions of regret and pseudo-regret. VAE has no notion of regret.
$\psi$-concentration of the sample mean, the core UCB tool. VAE relies on Monte Carlo expectations without exponential tail bounds.
Bounded-rewards UCB regret bound. No counterpart in VAE.
Pinsker / log-bound on Bernoulli KL, used in the LR85 lower bound. Not used in paper B.

Inverse-propensity-weighted semi-bandit loss estimate $\tilde{\ell}_t(i) = \ell_t(i) v_t(i)/x_t(i)$. VAE's gradient estimators are pathwise (reparameterization) and importance-weighting in EP14.2 is the score-function estimator the paper explicitly avoids; the inverse-propensity bandit estimator and the REINFORCE-style score-function gradient are different objects with different roles.
Ball-bandit unbiased loss estimate. No counterpart in paper B.

Two-point and one-point spherical-smoothing gradient estimates for zeroth-order bandit feedback. VAE's reparameterization gradient (TP14.1) is a fundamentally different first-order pathwise estimator that requires access to $\nabla_\theta \log p$, not function values at perturbed query points.
$(\alpha,\psi)$-UCB optimism-in-the-face-of-uncertainty index policy. No counterpart in VAE.
Exp3 and Exp3.P exponential-weights randomized forecasters. VAE's AEVB is an SGD on a likelihood lower bound, not an exponential-weights / expert-aggregation algorithm.
$\mathcal{S}$-Exp3, Exp4, and VE algorithms for contextual / expert / VC-class bandits. No analogue in paper B.
Banditron multiclass perceptron variant. No counterpart in VAE.
Exp2 with John's exploration for linear bandits. Absent in paper B.

Online Mirror Descent (OMD), its stochastic variant OSMD, and OSGD. These are online-learning algorithms with adversarial regret guarantees and Bregman-projection geometry; they have no counterpart in VAE training. Although AEVB is also a stochastic-gradient procedure, it operates on a fixed offline objective (the ELBO of an i.i.d. dataset) with no adversarial comparator and no regret guarantee, so the alignment is at best generic 'both use SGD' and is not meaningful.
Stochastic Golden Search for unimodal stochastic bandits. No counterpart in paper B.
Pseudo-regret bound for $(\alpha,\psi)$-UCB. VAE proves no such bound.
Pseudo- and high-probability regret bounds for Exp3 / Exp3.P. Absent in paper B.
$\Omega(\sqrt{nK})$ minimax adversarial-bandit lower bound. No analogue in VAE.
Contextual / expert / best-context-set regret bounds. No counterpart in paper B.
VE regret bound for stochastic contextual bandits with VC-dim policy class. No counterpart in VAE.
Banditron mistake bound. No counterpart in paper B.
Pseudo-regret of Exp2 with John's exploration for linear bandits. No counterpart in paper B.
OMD / OSMD regret bounds. Absent in VAE.
OSMD regret bounds for combinatorial / semi-bandit feedback (negative-entropy regularizer; $0$-potential / INF). Absent in paper B.
OSMD on the Euclidean ball, log-barrier regularizer. No counterpart in VAE.

OSGD regret bounds with two-point and one-point bandit feedback for nonlinear convex losses. The spherical-smoothing zeroth-order estimators have no counterpart in VAE's reparameterized first-order Monte Carlo gradient.
Pseudo-regret of Stochastic Golden Search for unimodal stochastic bandits. No counterpart in paper B.
Biased gain estimate concentration lemma for Exp3.P. Absent in paper B.
Stochastic-adversary lower bound lemma. No counterpart in VAE.
Properties of $F_\psi$ for $0$-potentials (Legendre / dual Bregman bound). Absent in paper B.

Divergence-theorem and Stokes-style smoothed-gradient identities used to justify the spherical-smoothing zeroth-order estimators. VAE's change-of-variables (PSP14.1) is a different identity (push-forward of densities under a diffeomorphism in latent space, not a divergence-theorem / surface-volume relation).
Two-point loss vs. smoothed loss inequality for nonlinear bandits. Absent in paper B.
SGS bracket retains the mode w.h.p. No counterpart in VAE.

All paper-A proofs (UCB / Exp3 / Exp3.P / lower bound / contextual / VE / Banditron / Exp2-John / OMD-OSMD / semi-bandit / ball-bandit / OSGD two/one-point / SGS) are regret-bound or concentration arguments specific to bandits and online learning. None corresponds to any proof in paper B (whose proofs PP14.1-PP14.3 derive the reparameterized Monte Carlo identity, the Gaussian-Gaussian closed-form KL, and the harmonic-style marginal-likelihood estimator).
Open problem on the optimal stochastic-bandit regret. No counterpart in VAE.
Latent-variable generative model $p_\theta(z) p_\theta(x|z)$. Paper A has no notion of latent variables, generative models, or i.i.d. data; its objects are arms / actions and loss/reward sequences.
Recognition model / probabilistic encoder $q_\phi(z|x)$. No counterpart in paper A.
Probabilistic decoder $p_\theta(x|z)$. Absent in paper A.
Variational lower bound (ELBO). Paper A's regret-minimization objectives are not lower bounds on a marginal likelihood and there is no KL-to-true-posterior decomposition in any of its theorems.

Reparameterization $\tilde z = g_\phi(\epsilon, x)$ of the variational posterior. Paper A's perturbed-play schemes (e.g. $X_t^\pm = x_t \pm \delta S$, ball-bandit perturbations) are sphere-uniform query schemes for zeroth-order gradient estimation, not reparameterizations of a parametric distribution; the goals (low-variance pathwise gradient through a learned distribution vs. unbiased gradient estimate from function-value queries) are different.
Bernoulli MLP and Gaussian MLP encoder/decoder parameterizations. Absent in paper A.
ELBO in KL+reconstruction form. No counterpart in paper A.

SGVB estimators ($\tilde{\mathcal{L}}^A$, $\tilde{\mathcal{L}}^B$, minibatch). These are Monte Carlo estimators of the ELBO; paper A's loss estimators (e.g. EP17.6, EP17.7) are inverse-propensity bandit estimators of adversarial losses with completely different role and structure.
Closed-form Gaussian VAE objective. Absent in paper A.
Full-VB shorthand $f_\phi(x,z,\theta)$. No counterpart in paper A.

Reparameterized Monte Carlo expectation theorem (change-of-variables identity for expectations w.r.t. $q_\phi(z|x)$). Paper A's Monte Carlo identities (e.g. LP17.7, LP17.8) are spherical-smoothing / divergence-theorem identities, not push-forwards of reparameterized samples through a parametric encoder; the cross-paper match is at best a generic 'Monte Carlo expectation' label, not a structural alignment.
Closed-form KL between two Gaussians (with $\mathcal{N}(0,I)$ prior). Paper A uses Bernoulli KL (DP17.2) for asymptotic regret lower bounds, an unrelated use of relative entropy.

Proofs of TP14.1 (reparameterized Monte Carlo via change of variables), TP14.2 (Gaussian-Gaussian closed-form KL), and AP14.2 (harmonic-style marginal-likelihood estimator via Bayes' rule). None of these proof techniques appears in paper A, which is dominated by union-bound + concentration + Bregman / Pinsker-style regret arguments.

Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes (AEVB) algorithm: SGD on the SGVB minibatch ELBO estimator. Paper A's bandit / OMD / OSMD / OSGD / SGS algorithms all target sequential regret minimization with feedback structure (full-information vs bandit, stochastic vs adversarial); AEVB is an offline batch-i.i.d. likelihood-maximization procedure with no exploration / regret component.
Marginal-likelihood importance estimator (gradient-based MCMC + density fit + harmonic-style inversion). No counterpart in paper A.
Full Variational Bayes AEVB (variational inference jointly over $z$ and $\theta$). Absent in paper A.
